sources.entry: Shlink - URL shortener with REST API and command line interface. Includes official progressive web application and docker images. (Source Code, Clients) MIT PHP/Docker
Shlink | URL shortener with REST API and analytics

summary.one_liner: Shlink is a self-hosted, PHP-based URL shortener that serves shortened links under your own domain, with a REST API and a command line interface.
summary.what_it_does: Shlink shortens URLs and serves them under a domain you control. It provides a REST API and a command line interface (bin/cli), and most operations are available through both, except API key management, which is CLI-only. The README says a web client is provided that can be used directly or self-hosted. Installation uses a pre-built dist zip or a build from source via build.sh, followed by an interactive installer (vendor/bin/shlink-installer). The README also describes an official Docker image configured through environment variables. It supports MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, Microsoft SQL Server and SQLite.
use_cases: Shorten links under my own domain
Manage short URLs through a REST API
Create and manage short links from the command line
Run a URL shortener in Docker
how_to_run: Download the shlink*_dist.zip file for your PHP version from the latest release and decompress it
Or clone the repository and run ./build.sh <version> to build a dist file
Grant write permissions to the data directory
Run vendor/bin/shlink-installer install on the server where Shlink will be hosted
Generate an API key with bin/cli api-key:generate
stack: MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, Microsoft SQL Server or SQLite (via pdo extensions)
notable: Official Docker image configured with environment variables
Full CLI and REST API with mostly equivalent operations
Optional RabbitMQ integration and RoadRunner support
caveats: Requires PHP 8.4 or 8.5 with several extensions (json, curl, pdo, intl, gd, gmp/bcmath)
The installer must be run directly on the server where Shlink will be hosted
API key management is only available from the command line
